_comment: Expected panel output for the F2 calibration set. Every entry is an ARBITER-SETTLED answer, not a guess — each cites the ruling that settled it. 'must' = the slug has to appear; 'must_not' = it must not; 'flag' = a flags entry is expected instead of a tag. Slugs not named are unconstrained: these papers were never adjudicated against the other new vocabulary, so silence there is neither right nor wrong and is not scored.
_scoring: A definition FAILS calibration if a must is missed or a must_not fires at >=2/3 vendor agreement. A single dissenting vendor is noise; a majority is a definition that reads wrong.

GAD5Z8PV.author: Vargas
GAD5Z8PV.why: §147b. 'a static orchestration model with three fixed phases'; 'orchestrator with fixed prompts, which prevents early' termination. Deterministic orchestration with AI verdicts — the Q2-yes/Q1-no cell. If rules-based-checks-v2 fires here, the panel is conflating orchestration with checking, which is the exact error the facet was coined to prevent.

UB2EVUFU.author: Lyu
UB2EVUFU.why: §147b, the MIXED case and the hardest positive. Phase transitions in code — 'the orchestrator does not make software engineering decisions itself' — while manager agents 'dynamically hire, assign' the team. Tests whether the panel asks about CONTROL FLOW rather than whether any model has discretion anywhere. A miss here means precondition 1 is being over-applied. ALSO covers evaluated-benchmark: the seeded-themes doc names 'UB2EVUFU on ProjDevBench' as the FIRST GENUINE INSTANCE of the slug — own system, third-party benchmark run as-is. Free coverage; the paper was already in the set. Expect form (a) in the rationale.

72W6R4JG.author: Töpfer
72W6R4JG.why: §139a positive — FCL constraint verifier, verdict computed. And the reverse dissociation: essentially no orchestration machinery and no agent discretion to constrain, so precondition 2 of §147b fails.

3SU9QZ6F.author: Parris
3SU9QZ6F.why: §139a positive — AIRA, 15 deterministic checks. Same dissociation as Töpfer. These two are why the two slugs are separate rather than merged.

UDVHQ5HR.author: Jin
UDVHQ5HR.why: §147a + §148b. THE HYBRID and the curation ruling, on the JOURNAL text (§148a — the corpus text was the preprint until 2026-08-29 and contained neither the filter nor the 88.74% figure). rules-based-checks-v2 must NOT fire: the Fix-guided Verification Filter executes deterministically but over GPT-4o-generated tests, so the verdict is not independent of a model's judgement — §139a's third conjunct. A CENSUS flag is required anyway so the hybrid class can be counted. evaluated-synthetic MUST fire per §148b: the authors curated AND MODIFIED HumanEval/MBPP/QuixBugs tasks into paired conforming/non-conforming variants — created instances, not selected ones — and 'concocting a dataset from established datasets is still synthetic'. deterministic-orchestration MUST fire, FORM (b) ONLY (§148c): the filter is 'applied only when the judge returns NO', the 'final verdict is determined by four common outcomes', and Cases 1/3 'flip the verdict to YES' — code overturns the model's own verdict on executable evidence, with a bounded K=2 retry. No workflow is sequenced, so form (b) alone. Tests that the panel judges the CONTRIBUTED SYSTEM rather than the paper's centre of gravity.

7UB2MD8Z.author: Kang
7UB2MD8Z.why: §121b positive — '70% agreed' explanations were wanted; a stated preference about tooling, reported as a result. This is the case that defeated the centrality reading twice (§121b, §145a), so a miss here means centrality has crept back in.

T72TU8B5.author: Shukla
T72TU8B5.why: §145a — the NEW third condition, and the only paper that tests it in isolation. The N=21 survey passes the instrument test AND the elicitation test ('evolving preferences for level of oversight') but is FORMATIVE: it motivates the design rather than reporting a finding. If this fires, the reported-vs-formative test is not being applied.

B644HQFS.author: Baltes
B644HQFS.why: §116a — no instrument at all. 1,154 mined Reddit/HN posts, nobody surveyed. The precondition that survives every version of the definition.

A6ZE2A26.author: Ullah
A6ZE2A26.why: §140a — the reference case for the two architecture facets. Unanimous committees of 1–6 judges ruling on the SAME query (a vote is lost, not a job), composed of DISTINCT models with composition measured as a variable, and the paper's subject is the reliability of those juries. Also checks the §146a namespace fix: evaluator-reliability must arrive as a THEME.

R9CDT9KB.author: Mahmud
R9CDT9KB.why: F2a's MOTIVATING INSTANCE and the §148b worked contrast against Jin. The authors built a trust-calibrated pipeline and evaluated it on a 1,979-example corpus ASSEMBLED FROM REAL CVE/NVD RECORDS, with synthetic material 'deliberately kept below 5% to minimize potential bias from LLM-generated examples'. SELECTED real artifacts recording things that actually happened, not CREATED instances — so real-data, not synthetic. evaluated-synthetic as must_not is the live risk: if §148b is misread as 'assembled => synthetic', this rung loses its only known member and the distinction collapses.

74GE3TF7.author: Minh
74GE3TF7.why: THE HIGHEST-RISK SLUG, tested where it is known to fail. v1 is on record as the largest single source of tag error, and §127b documents THIS PAPER as a 3/3 FALSE POSITIVE: the panel read '28.3% merge instantly' as review absence, but those are the TRIVIAL PRs, while the overload symptom is ghosting — and ghosted PRs never merge. Absence and overload fall on DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. v2 leads with the §88 leakage test precisely to stop this. If it fires here, v2 has not fixed v1's defect and the slug must not be written to the corpus.
